Location and internet features are off by default. Without them, CamperLog works completely offline.
Location (optional): only when you tap “Use current location”, CamperLog reads your position once and saves it with the stop. Never sent anywhere.

Track recording (optional, its own switch): off by default. Only after you start it on a tour, CamperLog reads your position at the interval you chose and saves the route with the tour, also while the screen is off. A permanent notification shows that it is running and lets you stop it. It never starts on its own and nothing is sent anywhere.

Weather & map (optional): CamperLog has the internet permission but only uses it when you turn this on. Getting the weather sends the stop’s coordinates, rounded to about 1 km, to Open-Meteo. The map loads the area you are looking at from OpenStreetMap. Searching for a place sends your typed text to OpenStreetMap Nominatim. All three services see your IP address.

Notifications (optional): off by default. Turning them on asks for the notification permission and runs a daily background check for due maintenance and your backup reminder, entirely on your device. For that check the app also holds two permissions granted at installation without a prompt: starting again after a restart and briefly keeping the device awake; they are only used while notifications are on. Nothing is ever sent anywhere.
No account, no ads, no analytics. Nothing else ever leaves your device.

Google plans to require every Android app — including ones installed outside the Play Store, like this one — to come from a verified developer identity, starting in 2026. Without that verification, devices will refuse to install apps at all.

This would hit F-Droid especially hard: an independent, sideloadable app store like F-Droid may no longer be able to exist in its current form, and continued maintenance of CamperLog outside Google's control could become impossible.

The "Keep Android Open" campaign is fighting these plans.

A tour is your whole journey, from starting it until you end it. Stops are the individual visits and overnight stays within that tour. CamperLog uses them to calculate travel days, nights, and distance.\n\nWhile a tour is ongoing, you can optionally start its GPS track. It records your route only after you start it, stays on this device, and can be stopped or deleted anytime.

resources.string: To save power, Android is allowed to pause apps that keep working in the background. A recording can then end mid-drive without telling you. If you exempt CamperLog from battery optimization, it keeps recording until you stop it. Recording is switched on either way.
